Definition: to hear intelligently (often with implication of attention, obedience, etc.; causatively, to tell, etc.)
BiblicalUsage: Shama is the Bible's great word for hearing, and it means far more than sound reaching the ear. God heard the cry of His people in Egypt, Moses commanded Israel to hear that the LORD our God is one LORD, and Samuel answered the voice in the night, Speak, for thy servant heareth. Isaiah warns of a people who hear indeed but understand not, and the psalm promises that the righteous cry and the LORD heareth them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hearing is the first act of faith, because faith comes by hearing the word of God. God hears His people before they hear Him, and that is why their cry is never wasted. That is why I answer the way Samuel did, Speak, for thy servant heareth, and I listen before I speak.
